1: # wg-basic
     2: 
     3: Linux-native WireGuard appliance in one small Rust binary. Unprivileged
     4: `serve` owns the SQLite desired state and the management HTTP surface;
     5: privileged `netd` applies it to the kernel through typed local-IPC
     6: operations. The database is authoritative, kernel state is reconciled
     7: from it, and `netd` never opens the database.
     8: 
     9: ## Quickstart
    10: 
    11: Needs Rust 1.89.0 (pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`) and loopback only —
    12: no root, no namespaces:
    13: 
    14: ```sh
    15: cargo build --locked
    16: install -d -m 700 [REDACTED_PATH]
    17: printf '%s\n' 'a strong administrator password' | \
    18:   cargo run --locked -- admin set-password --password-stdin \
    19:     --state [REDACTED_PATH]/state.db
    20: cargo run --locked -- serve \
    21:   --state [REDACTED_PATH]/state.db \
    22:   --socket [REDACTED_PATH]/netd.sock
    23: ```
    24: 
    25: In another terminal, check liveness, log in, and read back the session:
    26: 
    27: ```sh
    28: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz
    29: curl -s -c cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/login \
    30:   -H 'Host: 127.0.0.1:8000' \
    31:   -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8000' \
    32:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    33:   --data '{"username":"admin","password":"a strong administrator password"}'
    34: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/session -b cookies.txt \
    35:   -H 'Host: 127.0.0.1:8000' \
    36:   -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8000'
    37: ```
    38: 
    39: Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` for the operator UI, and stop `serve`
    40: with Ctrl-C (it drains, closes the database, and exits `0`).
    41: 
    42: `healthz` reports `degraded` here because no privileged `netd` is
    43: running — expected for the loopback demo. Real networking needs `netd`
    44: as root plus server setup; see
    45: [local netd](docs/development.md#local-netd) and
    46: [client enrollment](docs/client-enrollment.md).
    47: 
    48: ## Status
    49: 
    50: Network control, durable state/restart reconciliation, management/auth,
    51: product/enrollment/UI, and operational hardening are implemented and
    52: qualified in Linux namespaces. Native systemd installation and M004's
    53: update, rollback, and recovery transaction are technically qualified on
    54: current x86_64 and aarch64 GNU release artifacts. Phase 10 lifecycle
    55: qualification is closed, including fresh install, state-preserving
    56: uninstall/reinstall, and guarded purge. `v0.1.0` is released as a stable
    57: checksums-only build (unsigned, no trust root by maintainer decision):
    58: production `update check` and `update run` stay fail-closed, so every
    59: release needs a fresh install. See
    60: [plans/registry.md](plans/registry.md).
    61: 
    62: The `--version` release installer is a lower-assurance HTTPS/GitHub bootstrap.
    63: There is no signed-manifest installation path; verify downloads against the
    64: published SHA-256 digests — see [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)
    65: and [docs/release-signing.md](docs/release-signing.md).
    66:
